title: Gluten-Free Strawberry Cream Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft gluten-free cupcakes with real strawberry puree, ready in about 45 minutes total prep and bake time.
description: These cupcakes get their pink color from real strawberry puree, not food dye. I cook the puree down first so the crumb stays soft and the flavor stays bright, not watery. The gluten-free flour blend I use here bakes up tender, not gritty. You will not miss regular flour in this batch. The frosting is a simple cream cheese base tinted with a spoon of the same strawberry puree. It comes out a soft, natural pink, never neon. I tested this recipe three times in my home kitchen to get the crumb right. Fresh strawberries in season give the best color and flavor, but frozen work fine too.
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups fresh strawberries, hulled and chopped (about 8 oz)
1 3/4 cups gluten-free all-purpose flour blend (with xanthan gum)
instructions: Cook chopped strawberries with 1 tbsp sugar in a small pan over medium heat for 8 minutes, stirring often.
Mash the cooked berries, then simmer 2 more minutes until thick. You should have about 1/2 cup puree. Cool fully.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk gluten-free flour, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Beat butter and sugar until light and fluffy, about 3 minutes. Add eggs one at a time, then vanilla.
Add flour mix in three parts, alternating with buttermilk. Mix just until smooth.
Fold in 1/3 cup of the cooled strawberry puree, saving the rest for frosting.
Divide batter evenly among liners, filling each two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack.
Beat cream cheese and butter until smooth. Add powdered sugar gradually, then mix in remaining strawberry puree until frosting is soft pink.
Chill frosting 15 minutes if it feels too soft to pipe, then pipe onto fully cooled cupcakes.
tips: Cook the strawberry puree until thick and jam-like, or your cupcakes will turn out dense and wet.
Room temperature eggs and buttermilk blend into gluten-free batter more evenly and rise better.
If using frozen strawberries, thaw and drain extra juice before cooking down the puree.
Add puree to frosting a spoon at a time. Too much will make it too soft to pipe.

faq.question: Why does the frosting look pale pink instead of bright pink?
faq.answer: Real strawberry puree gives a soft, natural pink, not a bright dye color. That soft shade is normal and expected here, not a mistake.

faq.question: Can I use strawberry jam instead of making puree?
faq.answer: Fresh cooked puree gives better flavor and less added sugar. Jam works in a pinch, but skip the extra sugar in the frosting if you swap it in.

faq.question: Will this gluten-free flour blend work in other cupcake recipes?
faq.answer: Yes, as long as the blend has xanthan gum already mixed in. Blends without it need an extra 1/4 tsp added separately.

faq.question: Why is my batter thicker than a regular flour cupcake batter?
faq.answer: Gluten-free flour blends absorb more liquid than wheat flour, so a slightly thicker batter is normal. Do not add extra liquid to thin it.

conclusion: These cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can still taste like real strawberries, not a mix. Make the puree ahead of time and the rest comes together fast.
